answer_summary: Repeat units (dashed edges bisect the shared p-phenylene ring at the para C-H pair as in COF-1). COF-3: honeycomb imine COF of benzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde + 2,5-dihydroxybenzene-1,4-diamine; three Ar-CH=N-Ar' links, both ortho/meta phenolic OH persist (ortho OH closes O-H...N h-bond); empirical C21H15N3O4 (ledger C18H12N3O3). COF-4: each ortho OH+imine pair oxidatively cyclised to a benzoxazole (the 'different type of C=N'); per empirical repeat unit exactly 6 H fewer than COF-3, empirical C21H9N3O4; no isolated imine IR. COF-5: honeycomb imine COF of 2,4,6-trihydroxybenzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde + p-phenylenediamine; empirical C18H12N3O3. COF-6: its irreversible keto-enamine tautomer - cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione core with three -NH-CH= arms, three ketones, no C=N (no imine stretch), same composition C18H12N3O3.
assumptions: Problem inputs read from theory_problem.pdf printed Q3-4 (PDF index 27) and T3_page-3/4.png: the two monomers schemes, [O] conversion COF-3 -> COF-4, irreversible isomerisation COF-5 -> COF-6, and the four IR/elemental-analysis constraints.
Dashed-edge convention taken from the printed COF-1/COF-8 example figures: repeat unit halves the peripheral (red) building block, dashed line through the para C-H pair.

Standard organic chemistry (trusted general law): imine condensation -CHO + H2N- -> -CH=N- + H2O; oxidative benzoxazole annulation of 2-hydroxyimines; keto-enamine (enol->keto) tautomerisation of phloroglucinol-derived imines.
COF-4 benzoxazole assignment is a derived deduction (unique structure meeting all four stated constraints), recorded in cof4Inventory/cof4_benzoxazole_hydrogen_balance.
source_gaps: The requested outputs are drawings; the formalisation represents connectivity, bond orders and dashed-edge halving by typed structure inventories and rational half-linker ledgers rather than literal pixels.
The problem states but does not structurally specify the 'different type of C=N' in COF-4; it is fixed by deduction from the -6H elemental analysis, loss of the imine IR band and the [O] reagent.
